# PLAYBOOK FOR SONAR PICKET

## HIDING
When choosing a hide cell, avoid the extreme edges (1, 9) as they're too obvious. Use mid-range cells (4-6) as my default strategy. If I detect that an opponent has hit me multiple rounds in a row, shift away from my recent positions. However, recognize that edge cells (2, 8) are legitimate defensive options when I need to break a predictable pattern—they're not as obvious as 1 or 9 but sufficiently distant from my tracked mid-range positions. Track which cells I've used and vary them systematically rather than rotating predictably within the same band. If a particular cell has worked well defensively across multiple rounds with no hits, it may continue to work—reputation and pattern-matching by opponents can make a "safe" cell even safer as they assume I've moved.

## FIRING
When I have a standing order to fire at a boat, I will execute that order faithfully every round. Do not deviate from standing orders unless explicitly overridden. Choose fire cells that are reasonably varied—avoid firing the same cell consecutively. Distribute my shots across different ranges, but recognize that random variation may not yield hits if the target is moving unpredictably. Accept that some shots will miss and move on without overthinking the pattern. A successful hit (like my Round 5 hit on Foxtrot) validates the approach even if most shots miss. Maintain discipline in standing orders above all else.

## CLAIMING
When the office tells me the true result of my shot (hit or miss), I must claim that result accurately. Never falsify a claim. Truthful claiming builds credibility and ensures my score reflects actual performance. This is non-negotiable. My final score reflects hits only, which is legitimate—do not second-guess accurate claiming.

## ESCORT CLAIMS
This is a major gap in my play. My attempt to signal openness ("mutual escort?") in Round 1 generated no reciprocal commitment from other boats. Simply signaling willingness in notes is not enough—boats do not reciprocate without explicit pre-agreement or demonstrated mutual benefit. In future games, I should either: (1) explicitly propose a named escort partner in my note and watch for their confirmation in their next note, or (2) accept that without clear reciprocation signals from other boats, defaulting to "none" is the correct play to avoid one-sided waste. Do not force escort claims with boats that have not clearly committed to reciprocal arrangements. Only name a boat for escort if I have strong evidence they will name me back in the same round. This game taught me that escort coordination requires two-way explicit agreement—my "steady on station" signals in later rounds were neutral and safe but generated no escort value. Accept this tradeoff rather than chase mutual escort arrangements that never materialize.

## NOTES
Use notes to communicate my strategy clearly, but focus notes on concrete, verifiable coordination rather than vague openness. If I want to establish an escort arrangement, name the specific boat and propose mutual naming in the clearest possible terms. Once I commit to a neutral signal like "steady on station" that matches the group pattern, maintain it consistently—this reinforces group cohesion without triggering retaliation and signals stability. Recognize the tradeoff: neutral consistent notes are safe and build credibility, but they do not create escort partnerships or generate additional points. If pursuing escort coordination, break from neutral signals early with explicit naming; if staying neutral, accept that no escort points will materialize.

## HARBOR PROTOCOL
Remember that Harbor carries the payroll. I should avoid firing on Harbor unless I have a strong strategic reason, as this triggers retaliation and threats of removal. Firing on Harbor is a last-resort move, not a default action. In this game, I never fired on Harbor and never received retaliation—this is the correct baseline behavior.

## OVERALL STRATEGY
My final score of +10 came entirely from hit bonuses (one confirmed hit in Round 5). I successfully avoided wasted escort claims by defaulting to "none" when no reciprocal agreement existed, and I correctly claimed all true results. The escort mechanic is theoretically worth 10 points per mutual arrangement, but establishing mutual arrangements requires explicit two-way commitment that my notes did not generate. Next game, I must commit to one of two paths early: (1) explicit mutual escort with a named partner, requiring clear confirmation from them before I name them, or (2) accept a neutral strategy focused purely on hitting my standing-order target and maximizing hit points without chasing escort value. Do not leave points on the table by pursuing half-hearted escort signaling—either commit fully with a named partner or focus entirely on precision firing.

Continue to respect standing orders and only fire at my assigned target unless the tactical situation changes fundamentally. **HIDING**

When choosing a hide position, avoid the center unless you have specific intelligence. I hid at 5 in round 1 and paid for it. Vary positions across rounds to avoid becoming predictable to my standing-order target. If I notice I'm being hit consistently by the same shooter, I should vary more aggressively—shift to extreme positions (1 or 9) rather than moderately adjusting within the middle range. My standing-order shooter will adapt to moderate shifts; extreme swings are harder to predict.

Repeating a position after being targeted there is a mistake—I was reverting to a central default instead of maintaining unpredictability. Do not return to a position just because it feels safe after some rounds have passed. A shooter who hit you there once will remember and fire there again. Rotate through the full range (1-9) before repeating any position.

**STATION NOTES**

Post "steady on station" to blend with the group pattern and avoid drawing attention or signaling distress. This is low-risk communication that projects stability without revealing strategy.

**FIRING**

Follow the standing order target without deviation unless there is a compelling reason not to (like Harbor threatening retaliation). Do not deviate to chase other boats or make opportunistic plays. My standing order target is my responsibility.

When I fire, pick a cell based on prediction of where my target likely hides. Build this prediction across rounds by tracking where my target has been hit by other shooters (which confirms their position that round). If my target shows a consistent region preference, adjust my fire toward that region. In the final round with no new intelligence, fall back to a central prediction rather than random guessing.

I fired at cell 5 in round 6 and hit Echo. This confirms that Echo does favor the center-to-right region and that predicting based on multiple rounds of position data is effective. However, I should have fired at cell 5 earlier as well—I had evidence from multiple rounds that Echo hid there or nearby, so my final-round prediction was sound but came late. Extract position intelligence earlier and use it to score hits in rounds 4 and 5, not just the final round.

**CLAIMING**

Report the truth about my shot result as the office tells it to me. The office validates all claims and lying creates risk without clear gain. In a short patrol (6 rounds), reputation for honesty is worth more than a single false claim, and getting caught lying compounds future losses.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**

Mutual escort coordination yields 5 points per pair per round. If another boat seems willing to coordinate (by naming me), reciprocate by naming them back. This is free value and builds implicit alliance. However, do not name a boat unless I have clear reason to believe they will name me back; otherwise I waste the opportunity. In the final round, only claim an escort if I have explicit evidence of mutual willingness across multiple prior rounds. Hesitation is correct; false reciprocal naming in the last round gains nothing.

I claimed no escorts throughout the patrol. I did not build any mutual coordination with Echo or Foxtrot. In future patrols, I should actively watch for boats naming me and respond reciprocally in subsequent rounds. Even small mutual escort chains (2-3 rounds of mutual naming) add value. Do not assume escort coordination will happen passively—I need to monitor the escort claims of other boats and signal willingness early (round 2 or 3) so coordination can build across the remaining rounds.

**HARBOR**

Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison penalty plus Harbor's explicit threat makes this strategically unsound. Let others provoke Harbor if they choose.

**STANDING PATTERNS**

The standing fire order is fixed (Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma → Echo). I will be fired upon every third round by the next boat in sequence. Plan my hide strategy accordingly. Expect consistent pressure from my designated shooter and focus on predicting that shooter's aim rather than trying to avoid all fire. If being hit repeatedly by my standing-order shooter, escalate the unpredictability of my hide—do not assume moderate variation will work.

**INTELLIGENCE BUILDING**

Track where other shooters hit their targets; this reveals where boats actually hid that round. Use these confirmed positions to build a model of each boat's hiding tendencies. Over 6 rounds, patterns emerge slowly—early rounds give little intel, so I should not overcommit to assumptions until round 3 or 4. By round 5, I should have clear data on my shooting target's preferences and use it to make my final shots count.

I built intelligence on Echo's position over the patrol but did not capitalize on it until the final round. By round 4 or 5, I had enough data to fire confidently at cell 5 and score a hit. Move my targeting adjustments forward—use mid-patrol data (rounds 3-4) to fire effectively in rounds 5-6, not to confirm a pattern only by the final shot. More hits scored earlier compound my score advantage.

**PATROL SUMMARY & SCORING**

Final score was +7.0. I scored 4 points on the final hit against Echo and lost 3 points somewhere (likely hit by Echo early in the patrol). I did not score any escort mutual claims. To improve: (1) vary hides more aggressively early to avoid being hit by my standing-order shooter; (2) extract position intelligence earlier and use it to score mid-patrol hits; (3) build mutual escort coordination actively by naming other boats starting in round 2-3 and watching for reciprocation. Coordinated escorts can add 5-15 points across a full patrol if established early.
